featured_reviews.name: Lovie Chadha
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vasai Fort offers a fascinating glimpse into the region’s rich history while providing a peaceful escape from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. The fort has a unique charm, and walking through its ruins allows you to truly appreciate the stories and heritage it holds.

The atmosphere is calm and relaxing, and the scenic surroundings make it a wonderful place to spend a few quiet hours exploring, reflecting, and enjoying nature. Whether you’re a history enthusiast, a photography lover, or simply looking for a serene outing, Vasai Fort is definitely worth a visit.

humble request to all visitors: let’s help preserve the beauty and heritage of this remarkable place by maintaining cleanliness and avoiding littering. Small actions from each of us can make a big difference in keeping this historic treasure beautiful for future generations.

featured_reviews.name: Dipak Sapkale Koli
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Vasai Fort (also known as Forte de Baçaim during Portuguese rule), and it is truly a majestic yet neglected piece of history. There is no entry ticket, which makes it easily accessible for everyone. You will find local food stalls inside and around the fort offering vada pav, bhel, gola, and soda sharbat. However, visitors must ensure they do not litter and help keep this heritage site clean.

Built by the Portuguese Empire in the 16th century, it served as a strategic naval base, administrative center, and trading hub on the western coast. The fort remained under Portuguese control for nearly two centuries until it was captured by the Marathas under Chimaji Appa in 1739. Later, it passed into the hands of the British East India Company, marking another significant shift in power. Its construction reflects military brilliance, with a massive boundary wall stretching nearly 4 km.

Inside the fort, you can see magnificent church ruins, old barracks, market areas, bell towers, and beautifully crafted spiral stone staircases — all showcasing remarkable Indo-Portuguese architecture. The Mandwa Gate stands tall as a historic entrance, and the surroundings also include the revered Vajreshwari Temple and Hanuman Temple.

However, despite being under the Archaeological Survey of India, the site appears poorly maintained and largely ignored. Trees are growing out of the fort walls, weakening the structure, and no visible effort is made to clear them. Sadly, some miscreants have written their names on the walls, further damaging this heritage monument which is again ignored by Archeological Survey of India.

History needs to be cared for, restored, and respected — Vasai Fort deserves preservation worthy of its glorious past.

featured_reviews.review_text: Vasai Fort is a lovely, quiet spot to spend an evening. The historic ruins, dating back to the Portuguese era, is surrounded by greenery. It’s not crowded, making it perfect for a peaceful stroll or simply relaxing. The cool breeze and serene atmosphere make it a great place to unwind. If you're looking for a calm and scenic place to escape the hustle, Vasai Fort is definitely worth a visit.

It was eventually captured by the Marathas under Chimaji Appa in 1739.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently, I visited Vasai Fort with my friends. It is a historically significant site surrounded by lush greenery, offering a peaceful and scenic environment for visitors. The architecture and ruins reflect its rich past and make it an interesting place to explore, especially for history enthusiasts and photographers.

However, the maintenance of the fort requires considerable improvement. Several areas appear neglected, and better preservation efforts from the authorities would greatly enhance the overall experience.

Overall, Vasai Fort is a worthwhile destination for its heritage value and natural surroundings, but improved upkeep is necessary to fully realize its potential.

featured_reviews.name: Kushal Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5)
Vasai Fort / वसईचा किल्ला — Vasai West 🏰🌿

As someone born and brought up in Vasai, this place isn’t just a tourist spot for me — it’s a part of my life, my childhood, my memories, and my identity. 🫶
I’ve visited this fort more than 100–200 times, and every single visit still feels special.
वसईचा किल्ला holds a deep emotional place in every वसईकर’s heart. ❤️

This fort is vast, beautiful, historic and full of peace. 🌳
It’s surrounded by lush green trees on all sides, and one end of the fort touches the famous Vasai Dock. ⚓
If you’re into history, nature, photography, or even just calm vibes — this place is perfect. ☀️📸✨

History & Pride 🏹

This fort has seen the legacy of Marathas, Peshwas, and the Portuguese.
It is especially known for Chimaji Appa (brother of Bajirao Peshwa), who fought and reclaimed this fort back from the Portuguese. 🛡️🔥
The entrance itself greets you with his statue — a reminder of bravery and pride. ✨🗿

Why This Place is Special 🤍

I have come here with:

Friends 👬

Parents 👪

Cousins 👭

School picnics 🎒

Even solo, just for peace 🌿😌

For every phase of my life, this fort has always been there.

Cultural Importance 🎬

Many movies and songs have been shot here —
Most recently, a song from Kantara Chapter 1 was filmed here. 🎥
This place is loved by locals, tourists, and Mumbaikars alike. 🏞️

Must-See Inside 🔍

The massive stone walls 🧱

Huge open courtyards 🏞️

Old Portuguese structures 🕍

The Watch Tower – चक्री जिना (a must-visit + very photogenic 👀📸)

If you plan to explore the entire fort properly, keep at least half a day — it’s truly big. 🕒

Final Words 💛

This is not just a fort.
It’s a feeling. A memory. A connection. 🌙
If you are coming to Vasai — you cannot miss वसईचा किल्ला. 🌿

Highly recommended. 🤍
5/5 — Always. Forever. ⭐️

featured_reviews.name: Kushal Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
🌊 Suruchi Beach, Vasai | सुरुची बीच, वसई

I have been visiting Suruchi Beach since my childhood, as it’s barely 10–15 minutes from my home. It has always been the most convenient and special place for me — whether visiting with family or friends. ❤️

This beach honestly holds a special place in my heart. It’s my hometown beach, and it feels very personal and emotionally connected to me. 💞

✨ What I Love About This Beach

The fresh, clean air 🌬️

The smooth and cool sand 🏖️

The calm waves & cold water 🌊

The serene and peaceful view 🌅

The perfect place to enjoy sunrise and sunset — especially sunsets, which look absolutely magical here ✨😍

At the beach entrance, exactly opposite the shore, there’s a long line of tall, beautiful trees 🌲🌳 — almost like a small forest. It keeps the air fresh, breezy and adds natural beauty to the whole place.

Suruchi Beach is always lively with activities — volleyball, football, kabaddi, cricket, sketching, cycling and so much more 🏐⚽🏏🎨. Families enjoy picnics, kids play around, youngsters chill, and even people from outside Vasai come to visit.
Even in the evenings, when it’s full of people, the beach still feels peaceful and refreshing.

There are small food stalls near the entrance — bhel, pani puri, and other snacks 🍧🌯 — along with a small parking space for two-wheelers and a few four-wheelers, and rickshaws are easily available too.

❗The Only Negative

The only disappointing part is the garbage and plastic scattered here and there — wrappers, glass bottles, thermocol, and other waste 😞💔.
It’s heartbreaking to see people spoiling such a beautiful beach by not using dustbins.

VVCMC (वसई विरार महानगरपालिका) really needs to take stronger action — regular cleanups, installing dustbins, and appointing staff to maintain cleanliness. Proper care would make Suruchi Beach even better.

Apart from this, everything feels wonderful and refreshing every time I visit 🌿🥰.

⭐ Overall Rating: 4 out of 5 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐

featured_reviews.review_text:
🌊🏝️ Rangaon Beach, Vasai | रानगाव बीच वसई 🪨✨
Visited: Early Morning Ride (7:30 AM)

Yesterday, me and my friend decided to visit Rangaon Beach, and honestly — what an absolutely beautiful experience it was! 💙

We left home around 6:30 AM on our cycles 🚴‍♂️🚴‍♂️. The distance is roughly 8.5–9 km, so it took us about an hour to reach. And cycling during winter mornings when the temperature is around 14–15°C felt so refreshing, soothing, and energizing. That cool winter air while riding… just perfect. ❄️✨

When we reached the beach at around 7:30 AM, we parked our cycles easily — there’s plenty of open space for parking.

🌅✨ The Beach Experience — Just FABULOUS

I honestly don’t know where to start, because our experience was superb, fabulous, and beyond expectations.
This is the cleanest beach I have EVER visited.
Absolutely spotless — no plastic, no wrappers, no glass, not even a tiny bit of garbage anywhere. 🧡

A few years back, Rangaon Beach used to be dirty and polluted. But the Rangaon village people took a fantastic initiative, cleaned the entire beach, and continue to maintain it beautifully. Today, this beach stands as a benchmark for all other beaches — a true example of how a beach should be maintained. 🌟

Even the connecting road from the main city to Rangaon is super clean and well-maintained. Big appreciation to all the locals who keep this place so pure and peaceful. 🙏💛

🌊💛 Moments We Enjoyed

We walked along the beach for more than half an hour, took in the calm silence, and even sat on the stone embankment wall (mini stone wall) built at the side — a perfect spot to sit, relax, and enjoy the breeze. 🪨🌬️

We even stepped into the water, felt the cool waves touch our feet, and had our early-morning chats while standing in the sea. Trust me — pure therapy. 🌊🧘‍♂️💆‍♂️

All around us, even so early in the morning, people were:

walking 🚶‍♂️

running 🏃‍♂️

cycling 🚴

learning to ride vehicles 🚜

sitting with friends

relaxing

enjoying nature

There was life, but still complete peace.

🌤️💙 Why This Beach Feels Special

Cool & fresh early-morning air 🌬️

Crystal-clear sand 🏖️

Clean water 🌊

No garbage at all (literally ZERO!) ✨

Soothing atmosphere

Calm waves

Perfect silence

A refreshing energy you can feel

We didn’t even realize how one full hour passed. Our hearts kept saying — “Stay a little longer.” 💙

⭐ Final Thoughts

Rangaon Beach is PERFECT.
A flawless example of how a beach should be kept.
Clean, peaceful, natural, and maintained beautifully by the people of Rangaon village.

5/5 stars — fully deserved!
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Chimaji Appa formerly known as Bassein was the ultimate objective of the war, as this was the capital of the provincial government of Portugal's northern Indian
He was an able military commander who liberated the western coast of India from Portuguese rule. The high watermark of his career was the capture of Vasai fort from the Portuguese in a hard fought battle.
Chimaji was magnanimous in victory, and surviving Portuguese were given a safe passage from the city. Legends also speak of his emulating Shivaji Maharaj by returning with honor a woman of Portuguese governor's household who was presented to him as a spoil of war. Portuguese were given eight days to take all their movable property and move out. Accordingly, the last remnants of Portuguese army and administration pulled out of Vasai by 23 May 1739.

featured_reviews.name: Yaana Dalvi
featured_reviews.review_text: The Chimaji Appa statue, located in Vasai, Maharashtra, is a monumental tribute to the legendary Maratha warrior and Peshwa, Chimaji Appa. Unveiled in 2016, the 14-foot tall bronze statue stands proudly near the Vasai Fort, a historic site where Chimaji Appa led the Maratha victory against the Portuguese in 1739. Chimaji Appa, brother of Bajirao I, played a pivotal role in expanding the Maratha Empire. The statue is designed by sculptor Shri. Nitin Parekh. The statue depicts Chimaji Appa mounted on horseback, sword in hand, exuding confidence and strength. The monument serves as a reminder of Vasai's rich history and the Maratha legacy. The statue has become a symbol of Vasai's cultural heritage and a source of community pride.
